title: green-is-earned-not-assumed
intention: Red is the default; green is earned — Law 9 as derived physics, not prose a reader must remember to apply.
why: Akien, 2026-08-04: 'everything not working is red should have been one of the very first rules of our development. so i am so ruling now' + 'a newly minted IDEA is red until it's in code and running.' As prose it binds only the reader who remembers it, at the moment they remember it — which is exactly how a component came to sit for weeks describing a design its code did not implement. The lived symptom: a person reads a charter, believes the component works as described, builds on it, and discovers otherwise later.
traces_to: CP6 — 'The world is not a safe place. We have to build and care for safety as we go.' Ruled 2026-08-04 (2026-08-04-red-is-cp6-and-correction-needs-no-justification): Law 9 is CP6 turned on the corpus, not a new value. That matters to the BUILD, not just the filing — CP6's own falsifier language is the model to copy ('any drift between the code and this record is a red — physics, not a keep-in-sync comment'), and CP6 is already structurally present in every device and shim via CoreValuesMixin, which is the nearest existing carrier for a per-component green.

falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a component whose code stops matching its charter, or whose proof goes red, or which has never run, READS as red without anyone marking it — measured by breaking one deliberately and observing the change. AND when the surface can show a lot that has never been broken ground on, because a site plan that only knows about buildings already started is not a site plan. AND when a dependency change produces yellow (not red) in dependents, and self-cleaning via operational logs produces green without human intervention. WRONG INTENT if the answer turns out to be a field somebody sets; if the thing built reports on what EXISTS only — that reads green-by-omission, which is the precise failure the whole-site-starts-red framing is aimed at; or if every dependency change cascades red through the full chain.

how: Derive red/green from built + running + inspected, not from assumption. Build the derivation as a predicate over each component's charter, state, and proofs. No triage authority — everything starts red.

intent: Make Law 9 physics: a component is RED unless something measured says otherwise. Today Law 9 is prose in CLAUDE.md, which is policy — the thing Law 4 says is a tracked debt, not a resting state.
why_beneath_the_why: RULED SAME DAY (2026-08-04-the-spec-lives-in-akiens-head), and it changes what this ticket is building. Red is NOT a quality verdict — it is TRANSLATION DISTANCE. Akien: 'the picture in my head is the source of truth. it hasn't changed much in the last month. everything we talk about and make into tickets is trying to translate a pretty fixed spec in my head into english and thence to code. this source of truth in my head is why everything which is not that is red.' And the metaphor that makes it derivable: 'if this were a building site, anything slated for excavation would be red until its excavation was complete and had passed inspection. the whole building site starts red and slowly becomes green.' So the artifact this wants is closer to a SITE PLAN than to a health check — it must be able to show the lots nobody has broken ground on yet, which no test-result-derived signal can see. A component with no proofs, no code and no charter is the reddest thing on the site and is currently invisible to every scan we own.
mechanism: Three states, derived proportionally to the component's nature. GREEN: a certificate was issued with findings green at that point in time; the certificate is the unforgeable proof. RED: the component's own code or controlling data changed since its last certificate, or it has never been proved — must re-run and earn a new certificate through the gate. YELLOW: something the component depends on changed, but the component itself did not — it keeps operating; where logs exist and show correct function, it presents operational evidence at the gate and earns a new certificate without human intervention (self-cleaning). Simple components (basic sieves) that keep producing correct output do not need re-review when neighbors change. Components without logging stay at their last certificate until a problem is observed — human observation closes the loop, and the penalty for being wrong about a simple thing is small (CP5, CP6). There is no perfect safety; the system learns from the gaps.

BUILDME.need: derive red/yellow/green per component from: (a) certificate existence and validity, (b) own-code change since last certificate → red, (c) dependency change only → yellow, (d) operational logs showing continued function → self-cleaning yellow→green through the gate
the site-plan surface that shows unbuilt lots — components declared in the intentions but with no code, no charter, no certificate. The whole site starts red.

proportionality: simple components (basic sieves) do not need re-review when neighbors change as long as they keep operating correctly. The mechanism must not demand uniform observability from every component.

the_ladder: audit finds a sealed green whose proof no longer reproduces -> the seal is RED at that measurement (Law 9: measurement outranks approvals; nobody's ruling is waited for)
a competent agent (CC or Akien, today) attempts repair — a missed import, a moved path; fix, reprove, reseal green
repair fails -> trouble ticket (the trouble device already berths inspector findings; this is the same door)
no reproduced bug, only a suspicion the proof's claim no longer matches the spec -> back to design; important, not urgent
2026-09-06 seal audit disposition (Akien.cc_read: Not too lenient, on two conditions. (1) The color goes red at the measurement and stays red through every branch until reproven — design never restores green, so a peer cannot lean on it while we think (Law 8). Leniency would only be a component reading green while under design; the routing chooses who works it and how urgently, never the color. (2) The 'we merely think it might' branch is Akien's call, not CC's: a CC-declared 'this is a design question' is the paragraph the deterministic-red rule forbids. The repair attempt is bounded to changes that leave the proof's assertions untouched; anything that edits what was asserted is a change to what was proven and rides the ruling door. The audit is then not an alarm: red on the dashboard is loud (Law 7) and the trouble ticket is the permanent record; the system does not stop.
